contract.goal: the 3.0.0 shape of gRPC contracts and outbound tokens: contract modules inherit one parent and are checked by the gate instead of generated by a script; services map protobuf messages with MapStruct; one outbound token implementation shared by both client starters
contract.output: build/ludwig-grpc-api-parent, sources/outbound-token-core, sources/catalog-grpc-api, crud-service-example serving GetProduct over gRPC, contract checks in scripts/project_index.py, protobuf SPI on ludwig-service-parent's processor path, scripts/new_grpc_api.* deleted, token duplicates removed from rest-client and grpc-client, revapi exceptions, docs and CHANGELOG 3.0.0
constraints: every revapi.differences entry added names this change and its reason; no other difference is accepted
no existing test is changed to accommodate the gRPC server in crud-service-example
no existing mapper's generated code changes (task 6.2 stops otherwise)
rest-client keeps its configuration keys, SPI and exception messages
no rule is weakened, no test disabled, to make progress

decisions: rollback_point is the last commit; add-grpc-starters is implemented but uncommitted beneath this change, so a rollback to it also discards add-grpc-starters - revert this change's files instead

2.x: CachedToken keeps rest-client's semantics - a token with no stated expiry is treated as already expired. grpc-client's copy treated it as never expiring; the library's rule is the safer one its javadoc gives the reason for, so grpc-client's behaviour changes for an issuer that omits expires_in (unreleased module, no baseline)

2.3: ClientCredentialsTokenMinter takes the ClientRegistration (resolved by the caller, so rest-client keeps its own refusal messages) and accepts the OAuth2AccessTokenResponseClient as a constructor argument, which is what makes it unit-testable without a token endpoint; TokenMintingException names the registration and the OAuth2 error code

2.2: the moved CachingTokenSourceTest gained a forced-refresh concurrency case; its assertion is a bound (fewer mints than callers), not an exact count, because a forced caller that reads the generation after the new token is published legitimately mints again

3.1: rest-client resolves and narrows the registration itself (keeping its messages), mints through ClientCredentialsTokenMinter and rethrows TokenMintingException as the same IllegalStateException message as before; TokenRelayAuthenticationProvider reads the token through InboundBearerToken.of(Authentication), added to the library because rest-client's reactive path finds the authentication in the reactive context, not the thread's

3.3: two revapi.differences entries (java.class.removed for restclient.auth.CachedToken and CachingTokenSource), each justified with this change, the owner's decision and the replacement type. No public signature of ClientCredentialsAuthenticationProvider or TokenRelayAuthenticationProvider changed, so no further entry. Note: the semver block already permits breaking differences on a major increment; the entries are written because the root POM's rule asks every removal to be named

4.1: grpc-client's four token classes deleted; CachingTokenSource is built with Runnable::run as its async executor because gRPC applies credentials on its own executor and only the blocking path is used. The relay-capable SecurityConfiguration keeps its @ConditionalOnClass on AbstractOAuth2TokenAuthenticationToken by class NAME, so the module carries no type reference to it (TokenOwnershipTest)

4.2: TokenOwnershipTest was run red before the migration - 3 of 3 rules failed, naming grpc-client's CachedToken, CachingTokenSource, its minter's use of DefaultClientCredentialsTokenResponseClient and InboundToken - and green after

5.1: generation is bound in ludwig-grpc-api-parent inside a profile activated by ${basedir}/src/main/proto, not unconditionally: a pom-packaged parent that bound the generator would run it on itself and fail for want of a .proto. The profile is inherited and evaluated per module. Consequence: a contract module with no .proto would build an empty jar, so the layout check refuses one - a sixth contract check beyond the five design D2 lists

5.2: the contract checks are check_contracts(root) in scripts/project_index.py, run by manifest.sh layout; its self-test (manifest.sh self-test, project_index.py --self-test-contracts) builds each of 7 scenarios as a throwaway repository in a temp directory instead of committing fixture trees under scripts/testdata/ as the task wording said - the same both-fire-and-not-fire proof, with no 35 fixture files to keep in step with the POM shapes
5.3: scripts/new_grpc_api.sh and .py deleted; grpc-core's README (both locales) and CLAUDE.md describe the parent and the check instead

6.2: protobuf-spi-impl 1.47 on ludwig-service-parent's processor path after mapstruct-processor (version in ludwig-bom). Proof: the 7 generated mapper implementations of both services (crud: ProductDtoMapperImpl, ProductEntityMapperImpl; notification: Announcement/Notification/Inbox DTO mappers, NotificationEntityMapperImpl, InboxItemMapperImpl) are identical before and after, ignoring only MapStruct's @Generated date line; the SPI jar is confirmed on the compiler's processor path

7.2 (owner's decision): crud-service-example's role checks move from ProductController to ProductServiceImpl for get, search, update and delete, so REST and gRPC are gated by one annotation. Exception found while applying it: create keeps its check on the controller, because ProductImportHandler calls ProductService.create on a file-action worker with no caller (the file action checks the submitter's authority at submission) and a service-level role check would reject every deferred import row. gRPC serves only GetProduct, so it is fully gated. design D4, task 7.2/7.4 and a grpc-message-mapping scenario (PERMISSION_DENIED for a caller with no catalog role) were updated to say so

7.1: catalog-grpc-api's POM is the parent, relativePath, artifactId, name and description - 18 lines; its jar holds the generated Product, CatalogServiceGrpc and the .proto. GetProducts (batch) was added beside GetProduct so the example has a repeated field the service actually uses

7.2: grpc-core gains ru.ludwigandreas.grpc.core.mapping.ProtobufMapperConfig (@MapperConfig: NullValueCheckStrategy.ALWAYS, CollectionMappingStrategy.ADDER_PREFERRED, uses ProtobufConversions for Timestamp/Duration) so a service's protobuf mapper is @Mapper(config = ProtobufMapperConfig.class) and nothing more; mapstruct is an optional dependency of grpc-core and org.mapstruct.. was added to grpc-core's ModuleIndependenceTest allow-list with its reason, as that test's javadoc prescribes

7.2: the protobuf SPI needs its own annotation processor (no.entur.mapstruct.spi.protobuf.ProcessingEnvOptionsHolder) registered, because ludwig-service-parent lists its processors explicitly; added before MapStruct's. The 6.2 comparison was repeated after a mvn clean compile of both services with the processor registered: 7 of 7 mappers identical apart from the @Generated date

7.2: placement follows the service's architecture rules - CatalogGrpcService in web.grpc (an adapter, like a controller), ProductMessageMapper in web.mapper beside ProductDtoMapper, ProductBatch in service.model (a DTO may not hold service-model types). toModel ignores supplierCost explicitly (unmapped targets are an error in services)

7.2: ludwig-bom pins guava 33.6.0-jre, error_prone_annotations 2.50.0 and j2objc-annotations 3.1: with gRPC on a service's classpath they arrive by several paths at different versions and ludwig-service-parent's DependencyConvergence refuses that

7.3/7.4: the gRPC server runs in-process in crud-service-example's tests through src/test/resources/config/application.yml (in-process-name crud-service-example-${random.uuid}); no existing test changed. Base application.yml takes the TLS bundle from GRPC_TLS_BUNDLE with no default, so a deployment without TLS fails at startup; the local profile binds 127.0.0.1 and keeps authentication on (the X-Local-* backdoor is HTTP-only). Jib ports 8080/8081/9090 in the service's own pluginManagement. Suite: crud-service-example 21.4 s before, 24.4 s after (6 new gRPC tests)

7.4: CatalogGrpcIT authenticates with a @Primary test JwtDecoder whose tokens carry aud=product-catalog - the security starter wraps every JwtDecoder with the service's audience check, the test's included - and a named Converter class, because Spring MVC rejects a lambda Converter bean (no generic types)

8.1: owed-work notes about the duplicated token cache replaced by pointers to outbound-token-core in both grpc-client READMEs, rest-client's package map (both locales) and CLAUDE.md; outbound-token-core README in both locales; grpc-core README gained 'Mapping messages'; the root README lists the three new modules; CLAUDE.md and openspec/config.yaml describe ludwig-grpc-api-parent as a fourth POM

8.3: the changelog entries are under [Unreleased] (Added, Changed, and a new Removed marked as the reason the next release is 3.0.0), not under a dated [3.0.0] heading as the task worded it - the changelog's own preamble says a release is a tag and the heading is cut at release, so a 3.0.0 heading now would claim a release that does not exist
